It re-derives the nine columns, typed extents, carry ranges, reserved-skill-3 rule, full-int32 memory domain, typed InventoryLot(16384)/Job(8192) reference domains (kept distinct from EntityDirectory resident identity), paired-null and unbound-broken rules from the writers in work.gd and gear.gd; analyses lot/job binding uniqueness and concludes it is not a Work-intrinsic invariant and belongs to a saved cross-owner Work-Gear reconciliation; explicitly remaps the state_bytes diagnostic order (memory before XP) onto the canonical schema order (XP before memory); forbids construction/projection in the static API; designs a shape and canonical-source proof that kills the memory zero-substitution mutant rather than claiming value tests kill it; and recommends exact gate precedence, zero scratch, source-capacity pins and cycle avoidance, with ordinary runtime gaps listed separately as their own tasks. # Work owner16 local validator — independent feasibility review

2026-09-20. Read-only review of the proposed owner16 `work` local column predicate. No
implementation, no author dispatch, no acceptance. Every statement below is re-derived from the
writers in `godot/scripts/core/work.gd` and `godot/scripts/core/gear.gd` at the pinned digests in
`source-sha256.json`, not carried over from the discovery note. Verify against those files again
before any contract is frozen.

## 1. Re-derived column set and extents

`_allocate_columns()` sizes exactly nine columns, and `clear()` writes exactly those nine plus the
derived `_bound_tool_count` and the per-tick scratch. `RESIDENT_CAPACITY` is borrowed from
`needs.gd` and `SKILL_COUNT` from `residents.gd`; the constructor asserts the residents capacity
equals `Jobs.AGENT_CAPACITY` and the skill count equals `Jobs.JOB_KIND_COUNT`. Canonical section-4
field order (`save_component_columns_schema.gd`, owner 16, version 2, primary 512, no child
extents) is:

| ordinal | field | type | elements |
|--:|---|---|--:|
| 0 | `_potential_remainder` | i32 | 512 |
| 1 | `_xp_remainder` | i32 | 6144 |
| 2 | `_memory_total` | i32 | 512 |
| 3 | `_wear_remainder` | i32 | 512 |
| 4 | `_tool_lot_slot` | i32 | 512 |
| 5 | `_tool_lot_generation` | i32 | 512 |
| 6 | `_tool_job_slot` | i32 | 512 |
| 7 | `_tool_job_generation` | i32 | 512 |
| 8 | `_tool_broken` | u8 | 512 |

Eight i32 columns totalling 9728 elements give 38912 bytes; the byte column adds 512, for 39424
packed bytes. `settlement_payload_bytes()` re-derives only the five settlement columns (10752), so
it is not the whole-image figure and must not be used as one. The 6144 XP extent is `512 * 12`, a
fixed derived stride, not an independent child extent — owner 16 declares zero child extents.

## 2. Re-derived value domains

- **Potential carry.** `_produce_potential()` writes `accumulator - produced * WORK_FACTOR_DENOMINATOR`
  with a nonnegative accumulator, so the domain is `0..999`.
- **XP carry.** `_credit_xp()` writes modulo `MILLI_WU_PER_WU`, so `0..999` per (resident, skill).
- **Reserved skill.** `_append_contributor()` gates on `_check_skill()`, which refuses index 3, and
  `_credit_xp()` is the only XP-remainder writer. Index `resident * 12 + 3` is therefore always 0.
- **Wear carry.** `_charge_tool()` stores either `carried` when below `GENERAL_WEAR_MWU_PER_POINT`
  or `_wear_outcome.remainder_after`, which `gear.gd` computes as `total % 10000`. Domain `0..9999`.
- **Memory total.** `set_memory_total()` accepts **any** signed int32 at **any** valid physical
  resident address, with no presence, liveness or sign test. Both extrema are legal values.
- **Broken.** `_charge_tool()` latches 1; `clear()` and `_clear_tool_binding()` write 0. Domain `{0,1}`.
- **Tool lot reference.** Written only by `claim_tool_for_work()` after `_gear.has_gear(lot_ref)`
  succeeded; `gear.gd`'s `_resolve_row()` admits only `0 <= slot < LOT_CAPACITY(16384)` and
  `generation > 0`. Unbound is exactly `(-1, 0)`.
- **Tool job reference.** Written from `_jobs.job_of(resident_slot)` after `claim_for_job()`
  accepted it, and `gear.gd`'s `_check_job_ref()` admits only `0 <= slot < JOB_CAPACITY(8192)` and
  `generation > 0`. Unbound is exactly `(-1, 0)`.

**These are typed-store references, not Directory identities.** The lot bound is `Inventory`'s lot
space and the job bound is the `Jobs` row space; neither is `EntityDirectory.DIRECTORY_CAPACITY`.
Resident ownership is resolved separately, through `_directory.get_typed_row(_gear.owner_of(...))`,
and that Directory reference is never stored in any Work column. Any validator that bounded the lot
or job slot by the directory capacity would be wrong in both directions.

**Paired null.** `_clear_tool_binding()` writes all four reference halves and the broken byte
together, and `claim_tool_for_work()` writes all five together. So per row: lot slot null iff lot
generation 0 iff job slot null iff job generation 0, and an unbound row has broken 0. A bound row
may legally be broken 1. Half-null pairs are unreachable and should be refused, matching the
stronger posture `gear.gd`'s own `_gear_active_row_refusal()` already takes for its refs.

## 3. Rules that must NOT be tightened

- **No absent-row rule.** Nothing keys any Work column on presence, and `set_memory_total()` writes
  any address. There is no "blank row" canonical form analogous to `gear.gd`'s `_blank_row()`, so a
  nonzero carry or a nonzero memory total on an unoccupied resident address is legal data.
- **No living-256 cap.** The GDD living-population cap governs modelling, not this physical 512-row
  extent. A predicate that refused rows above 256, or counted "live" rows, would invent a rule.
- **Carries survive release.** `release_tool_claim()` and `_clear_tool_binding()` deliberately do
  not touch `_wear_remainder`, and no path clears `_potential_remainder` or `_xp_remainder` except
  `clear()`. An unbound row with a large nonzero wear carry is the expected mid-point state.
- **Stale current-job history is data, not damage.** A worker who changed job keeps the older
  binding until an explicit release; `_tool_gate()` reports `TOOL_CLAIM_BELONGS_TO_ANOTHER_JOB` at
  tick time. A saved-image validator has no live `job_of()` to compare against, must not acquire
  one, and must not normalise or repair the retained reference.

## 4. Uniqueness of lot and job bindings

Neither binding is a pure intrinsic invariant of this owner's columns.

*Lot.* Two Work rows holding the same lot reference would require two successful
`claim_tool_for_work()` calls without an intervening release. The first is refused by
`_check_tool_binding_target()` (`TOOL_ALREADY_CLAIMED`) only for the *same* resident; for a second
resident the refusal comes from `gear.gd`'s `claim_for_job()` (`GEAR_ALREADY_CLAIMED`), and
additionally `_check_tool_binding_target()` requires the recorded gear owner to resolve to that very
resident row. So the guard lives in **Gear's** claim columns, not in Work's. No Work-local writer can
reach a duplicate, but the witness of that fact is external state this predicate cannot see.
Enforcing it locally would be either redundant (when the Gear image is consistent) or actively
misleading (it would attribute a Gear claim-column corruption to owner 16). Recommendation: exclude
it, and record Work-to-Gear claim reconciliation — lot resolves, claim held, claim job equals the
Work job reference, gear owner resolves to this resident — as a saved cross-owner check.

*Job.* `claim_for_job()` keys on the lot and permits one job to hold several lots, so identical job
references across Work rows are not even structurally forbidden; they depend entirely on whether
`jobs.gd` admits two agents on one job row. No uniqueness rule should be asserted here at all.

A secondary reason to defer: a local lot-uniqueness pass needs a 16384-byte bitmap, which is the
only scratch this predicate would otherwise require. Dropping it keeps the scratch at zero.

## 5. Byte-order remap between the diagnostic and the canonical image

`state_bytes()` appends potential, **memory**, **XP**, wear, lot slot/gen, job slot/gen, broken. The
canonical schema order is potential, **XP**, **memory**, wear, and the rest. The two differ only in
the swap of ordinals 1 and 2, and the blocks are different lengths (6144 vs 512 i32), so a fixture
built from a runtime `state_bytes()` image must be remapped explicitly: diagnostic block 2 (bytes
2048..4095) is canonical field 2, and diagnostic block 3 (bytes 4096..28671) is canonical field 1.
Do not change the established diagnostic order — it is an existing byte-identity comparison used by
refusal tests — and do not let a test silently feed the diagnostic image to a canonical-order API.

## 6. Construction, projection and scratch

`Work._init()` builds a `Jobs` store when none is supplied, and that store in turn owns residents,
needs and the directory. A validator that called `WorkScript.new()` would allocate an entire
collaborator graph. The API must therefore be **static**, take the nine columns as nine explicit
typed arguments in canonical order, construct nothing, and build no projection or per-row object;
the caller's frozen copy-on-write buffers are read in place. With uniqueness excluded, the predicate
needs no scratch buffer at all, and the existing one-owner streaming allowance covers the 39424
caller bytes with no new allocation row. Follow the owner-15 bridge shape
(`save_owner_transforms.gd`): null record, owner index, forwarded `Schema.schema_refusal()`, this
owner's pinned metadata, forwarded `Section.owner_shape_refusal()`, then the typed accessors, then
the raw column code.

## 7. Recommended gate precedence

First failing gate wins; refusals are deterministic and carry no row identity.

1. All nine argument extents, in canonical order (512, 6144, 512, 512, 512, 512, 512, 512, 512).
2. Potential carry `0..999` over all 512 elements.
3. XP carry `0..999` over all 6144 elements, then reserved-index-3 XP equals 0 for all 512 residents.
4. Memory total: **no gate**. Every signed int32 is accepted, and this is stated explicitly rather
   than omitted, so a later reader cannot mistake the absence for an oversight.
5. Wear carry `0..9999`.
6. Broken byte `0..1` across the whole extent, checked before any row's meaning depends on it.
7. Lot reference shape: exactly `(-1, 0)`, or slot `0..16383` with generation `> 0`.
8. Job reference shape: exactly `(-1, 0)`, or slot `0..8191` with generation `> 0`.
9. Cross-column: the four reference halves null together, and an unbound row has broken 0.

Pin `RESIDENT_CAPACITY`, `SKILL_COUNT`, `SKILL_RESERVED_INDEX`, `WORK_FACTOR_DENOMINATOR`,
`MILLI_WU_PER_WU`, `GENERAL_WEAR_MWU_PER_POINT`, `Gear.LOT_CAPACITY` and `Gear.JOB_CAPACITY` by
reading the owning constants, and additionally pin the literal contract values so a silent capacity
change refuses. **Cycle:** a bridge may preload `work.gd` and `gear.gd` (neither preloads a
validator); nothing in `gear.gd`, `jobs.gd` or `inventory.gd` may preload the new module, and no new
immutable `Array` constant should be introduced.

## 8. Killing the memory zero-substitution honestly

Because the memory domain is the whole of int32, a mutant that replaced the memory argument with a
zero-filled array of the same length is **semantically equivalent** for a domain-only predicate. No
value test can kill it, and claiming one does would be false. Kill it with shape and canonical-source
witnesses instead: (a) supply a memory column of the wrong extent (511, 513, 6144) and require the
shape gate to refuse — a substitution that synthesises its own 512 zeros accepts; (b) supply the XP
and memory arguments transposed and require refusal, which the differing extents make decidable;
(c) assert the compiled metadata for ordinal 2 is key `_memory_total`, type i32, elements 512, and
ordinal 1 is `_xp_remainder`, i32, 6144, so the canonical mapping is pinned in the test rather than
inferred. The mapping itself remains source-reviewed; a wrong extent is what makes it witnessable.

## 9. Test coverage the contract should require

Every physical row and both tails of each column; every range endpoint and the first value outside
it; both malformed reference halves for lot and job independently; a valid bound row and a valid
unbound row each carrying large retained carries; both signed memory extrema; a bound-and-broken
row accepted; reserved-skill XP nonzero refused; all nine wrong-shape witnesses; exact refusal
precedence where two gates could both fire; and complete non-mutation of all nine caller arrays
across accept and refuse. Public runtime fixtures should exercise existing work, XP and wear
behaviour, release and reclaim, and retained stale-current-job history, then compare exact bytes,
public readers and the diagnostic image around a validation call.

## 10. Ordinary runtime gaps — separate tasks, not validator business

These are defects or absences in production behaviour. None of them may be normalised, repaired or
papered over by a local column predicate; each needs its own task.

- The productive tick does not read `jobs.tool_gate_of()`, so a tool-required job whose worker holds
  no binding produces work and wears nothing.
- No passive-wait flag exists on the Job row, so an actively worked WORK tick and a passive wait are
  indistinguishable to this module.
- No MoodMemory store exists; `_memory_total` is an explicit caller input defaulting to 0.
- `_bound_tool_count` is derived, is not part of the canonical image, and has no rebuild path.
- Purpose restoration from completed useful labour is unwired.

## 11. Deferred

Bulk capture/restore and the `_bound_tool_count` rebuild; saved Gear/Inventory/Jobs/resident
identity, claim uniqueness and lifecycle/provenance within one file; coordinator invocation; full
persistence and publication. An accepted local result certifies column shape and domain only. It is
not a playable world, not a cross-owner consistency claim, and not a cross-world contamination
detector.
